title: Start small, save often
description: Saving $2 regularly beats waiting to save $50 someday — here is why small wins.

body.heading: Small is not pointless
paragraphs: It is easy to think saving only counts in big amounts. But $2 a week is over $100 in a year, and more importantly it builds the habit and the identity of someone who saves.
Choose an amount so small you will not miss it, and move it on a set day. When it feels easy, nudge it up a little.

body.heading: Make it automatic
paragraphs: Saving works best when you do not have to remember or decide each time. If your account allows an automatic transfer on payday, even a tiny one, the habit runs itself.
If automatic is not an option, pair saving with an existing routine — after your shift, on Sunday evening, whenever you check your balance.

body.heading: Watch it grow
paragraphs: Check your savings occasionally and enjoy the progress. Seeing a balance climb from $10 to $60 is motivating in a way that advice alone never is.

takeaway: Save a tiny amount on a regular day, make it automatic if you can, and let it grow.
